contexts.text: He was mighty in hunting before Jehovah () = that he had persuaded many; for such is the nature of faith separated from charity.

To hunt, in the Word, in general = to persuade; in special, to captivate minds by flattering their sensuals, pleasures, and cupidities by using doctrinal things, which they explain according to their inclination and that of the other at their pleasure, for the sake of self... Illustrated.
To hunt () = to deceive by persuasions, and by Knowledges, which they pervert, and which they explain in favour of self, and according to the inclination of the other.
To hunt () = to insidiate for the sake of self, or to call falsity truth, and to utter perversity and wrest, so persuading.

Esau was a man knowing in hunting () = the good of life from sensuous and scientific truths... Hunting = the truths themselves, but the truths which are of the natural man from which are goods... which are called scientifics; and scientifics are of two kinds or degrees, namely, sensuous and scientific things: by hunting, here, both are signified. Sensuous things are those in which children are; scientifics are those in which the same are when they grow up...

The reason by hunting are signified the sensuous and scientific truths in which they who are in the good of life are taught and with which they are affected, is because hunting in a wide sense = the things which are taken by hunting; as rams, kids, goats, and the like, which = spiritual goods... and because the weapons of hunting, which were quiver, bow, and missiles = the doctrinal things of truth. Illustrated.
Hence it is that to hunt = to teach, and also to persuade; and this in both senses; namely, from the affection of truth, and from the affection of falsity. Illustrated.
Hunters = those who teach from scientific truths, and also from doctrinal things.
To hunt in the field = to persuade from the affection of falsity.
Nets are wont to be attributed to this kind of hunting.
Isaac loved Esau because venison was in his mouth () = that the Divine good of the Divine Rational loved the good of truth... Venison = the good of life from natural truths.
Hunt venison for me () = the truth of good. To hunt, and venison = the truth of the Natural from which is the good of life; here, the truth which is from good, because it is said to Esau...

Esau went to the field to hunt venison, to bring it () = the endeavour of the affection of good to procure truth which might be conjoined with the Divine Rational... Venison = the truth which is from good.
Bring me venison () = the truth of good.
Sit down and eat of my venison () = the truth of the affection of such good... Venison = the truth which is from good.
This good and this truth (of the Natural) are what are represented by Esau and his venison.
I will eat of my son's venison () = the longing to conjoin with itself natural truth by means of good... My son's venison = the truth of good.
Esau his brother came from his hunting () = the truth of good and its advent... Hunting = the truth which is from good.
Eat of thy son's venison () = that it might appropriate to itself the truth of natural good... Venison = the truth of natural good.
Who is he that hath hunted venison and brought it to me? () = inquiry concerning that truth... Venison = the truth from good; here, inquiry concerning this truth, as to whether it is from good.
To hunt them () = to instruct in the internal things of the Church.

That the Church is to be established from those who are in natural good and in spiritual good, is meant by, I will send fishers who shall fish them, and hunters who shall hunt them ()... To gather those who are in spiritual good, is meant by the hunters who shall hunt them. AE 513:12.
They hunt our steps () = to seduce by falsities.
